typeName: Rate in context from a table
title: Medicine in the blood: rates from data and from a model

stimulus.title: Concentration of a medicine
stimulus.html:
The concentration of a medicine in a patient's blood is modeled by a differentiable function CC, where C(t)C(t) is measured in milligrams per liter (mg/L) and tt is measured in hours after the medicine is taken. Selected values of C(t)C(t) are shown in the table.
Concentration C(t), in milligrams per liter, at selected times t, in hours
tt (hours)001133446688
C(t)C(t) (mg/L)007.47.412.212.212.012.09.99.97.37.3

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Use the data in the table to estimate C′(5)C'(5). Show the computations that lead to your answer, and indicate units of measure.

rubric.point: A difference quotient on an interval that contains <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 5</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{C(6) - C(4)}{6 - 4}</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C'(5) \approx -1.05</annotation></semantics></math> milligrams per liter per hour
accept: the units point needs the correct units with an answer

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>9.9</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>12.0</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C'(5) \approx \frac{C(6) - C(4)}{6 - 4} = \frac{9.9 - 12.0}{2} = -1.05</annotation></semantics></math> milligrams per liter per hour.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Interpret the meaning of C′(5)≈−1.05C'(5) \approx -1.05 in the context of the problem.

rubric.point: At time <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 5</annotation></semantics></math> hours, the concentration of the medicine is decreasing at a rate of about 1.05 mg/L per hour
accept: names the time, the quantity, decreasing, and the rate with units

"is changing at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1.05</annotation></semantics></math> mg/L per hour"

parts.sample: Five hours after the medicine is taken, the concentration of the medicine in the blood is decreasing at about 1.05 milligrams per liter per hour.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Must there be a time tt, for 1<t<31 < t < 3, at which C(t)=10C(t) = 10? Justify your answer.

rubric.point: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> is differentiable, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 \le t \le 3</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: must state continuity on the closed interval, with the reason

rubric.point: Yes: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>7.4</mn><mo><</mo><mn>10</mn><mo><</mo><mn>12.2</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C(1) = 7.4 < 10 < 12.2 = C(3)</annotation></semantics></math>, so by the Intermediate Value Theorem there is such a time
accept: the values and the theorem must both appear

parts.sample: Yes. <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> is differentiable, so it is continuous on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 3]</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>7.4</mn><mo><</mo><mn>10</mn><mo><</mo><mn>12.2</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C(1) = 7.4 < 10 < 12.2 = C(3)</annotation></semantics></math>, the Intermediate Value Theorem guarantees a time <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo><</mo><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 < t < 3</annotation></semantics></math> at which <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C(t) = 10</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: For 0≤t≤80 \le t \le 8, the concentration is also modeled by M(t)=10te−0.3tM(t) = 10te^{-0.3t}. Find M′(5)M'(5). Show the setup, and indicate units of measure.

rubric.point: Setup: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M'(5)</annotation></semantics></math>, with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.3</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.3</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M'(t) = 10e^{-0.3t} - 3te^{-0.3t}</annotation></semantics></math> or a calculator's numerical derivative at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 5</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M'(5) = 10e^{-1.5}(1 - 1.5)</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>10</mn><mi>t</mi><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.3</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left.\frac{d}{dt}\left(10te^{-0.3t}\right)\right|_{t = 5}</annotation></semantics></math>

rubric.point: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.116</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M'(5) \approx -1.116</annotation></semantics></math> milligrams per liter per hour
accept: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.115</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1.115</annotation></semantics></math> (truncated) or <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.116</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1.116</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.3</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.3</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.3</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>0.3</mn><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M'(t) = 10e^{-0.3t} - 3te^{-0.3t} = 10e^{-0.3t}(1 - 0.3t)</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow></msup><mo>≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.116</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M'(5) = -5e^{-1.5} \approx -1.116</annotation></semantics></math> milligrams per liter per hour, close to the estimate from the data.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: Using the model MM, is the rate of change of the concentration increasing or decreasing at t=6t = 6? Give a reason for your answer.

rubric.point: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">″</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.099</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M''(6) \approx -0.099</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: a calculator's numerical derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M'</annotation></semantics></math> at 6

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">″</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.3</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.9</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M''(t) = e^{-0.3t}(0.9t - 6)</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">″</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.6</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.8</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M''(6) = -0.6e^{-1.8}</annotation></semantics></math>

rubric.point: Decreasing, because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">″</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M''(6) < 0</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: the rate of change <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M'</annotation></semantics></math> is decreasing since its derivative is negative

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">″</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.099</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M''(6) \approx -0.099</annotation></semantics></math> (by differentiating <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M'</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">″</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.3</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.9</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M''(t) = e^{-0.3t}(0.9t - 6)</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">″</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.6</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.8</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M''(6) = -0.6e^{-1.8}</annotation></semantics></math>). Since <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">″</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M''(6) < 0</annotation></semantics></math>, the rate of change of the concentration, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M'</annotation></semantics></math>, is decreasing at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 6</annotation></semantics></math>.
